name: Ornithodesmus
isnote: Howse & Milner 1993 read it as a troodontid, Naish et al. 2001 as a ceratosaur or coelophysid, Naish & Martill 2007 as a dromaeosaurid (Wikipedia revision 1383347813).
sum: Small theropod from the Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, known from a fused sacrum first taken for a bird and later for a pterosaur.
wsnote: Known only from a sacrum; no body size in the sources consulted.
holotype: BMNH R187, a sacrum of six fused vertebrae found by the Rev. William Fox at Brook Bay, Isle of Wight; Wessex Formation.
material: Only the holotype. The pterosaur remains once referred to the genus (O. latidens) were later renamed Istiodactylus.
biology: The small thigh muscles are indicated by the size and anatomy of the sacrum; nothing more is stated in the sources.
author: Seeley 1887

sources.text: Harry Govier Seeley 1887. On a Sacrum, apparently indicating a new type of Bird, Ornithodesmus cluniculus, Seeley, from the Wealden of Brook. Quarterly Journal of the Geological Society. doi:10.1144/gsl.jgs.1887.043.01-04.19
S. C. B Howse, Andrew R. Milner 1993. Ornithodesmus―a maniraptoran theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of the Isle of Wight, England. Palaeontology.

dates_note: No PBDB record. Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, about 125 Ma (Wikipedia revision 1383347813); the Barremian ICS bounds are used.
